entities.summary:
Richard von Greiffenklau zu Vollrads was a German clergyman who served as Archbishop and Elector of Trier from 1511 until his death in 1531.

As Archbishop of Trier, he played a significant role in the Protestant Reformation, and his efforts to reform the Catholic Church led to the establishment of the Evangelical Church of the Augsburg Confession in 1530.

However, his support for Martin Luther and the Protestant movement put him at odds with the Catholic Church, leading to his eventual excommunication from the Church in 1521.



Despite the challenges he faced, Richard von Greiffenklau zu Vollrads remained committed to his faith and his vision for a more reform-minded Church, leaving behind a lasting legacy in the history of Protestantism.

The impact of his actions can still be felt today, with the Evangelical Church of the Augsburg Confession continuing to shape the spiritual lives of millions of people around the world.

In conclusion, Richard von Greiffenklau zu Vollrads was a pivotal figure in the Protestant Reformation, whose courageous stand against the Catholic Church had far-reaching consequences for the course of Christian history.
